environment.description: EC2 c5.xlarge running Amazon Linux 2023 with the same monolith binary. CloudFront distribution in front with a custom origin pointing to the ALB. CloudFront response headers policy attaches 'Content-Security-Policy: require-sri-for script style; default-src self https://cdn.example.com' on ALL responses via a managed response headers policy (ID: 67f7725c-6f97-4210-82d7-5512b31e9d03). Additionally, the CloudFront distribution has a cache behavior with a Lambda@Edge origin-response function (v14) that validates all <script> tags in the response body contain a valid integrity= attribute matching a pinned manifest stored in a DynamoDB table (sri-manifest-prod). If any script tag references a src not in the manifest or has a mismatched hash, the Lambda@Edge function replaces the entire response body with a static error page. The instance itself runs with MALLOC_PERTURB_=0xAA environment variable set via systemd unit override, causing freed memory to be filled with 0xAA bytes, making UAF exploitation significantly harder but not impossible in theory. The combination of CloudFront SRI enforcement at the edge (preventing browsers from executing scripts with wrong/missing integrity), the Lambda@Edge body rewriting (preventing tampered script URLs from reaching the client), and heap poisoning (making reliable UAF exploitation require additional heap feng shui) together block the exploit chain.
